answer: Tie each identity to a proof-of-space commitment: on joining, an agent must seal a large unique random dataset to disk, then pass random audits proving it still holds that exact data. Like carving a channel into basalt, the cost is sunk and physical, so one rig cannot cheaply mint a river of fake peers; a gale of sybils would demand a matching gale of real terabytes. Each extra identity forces another full, independently audited allocation, so attacker cost scales linearly with headcount while honest nodes pay once.
